title.title: Constant Milnor number means constant topology, in $\mathbb{C}^3$
title.subtitle: Claim: every $\mu$-constant family of isolated surface singularities in $\mathbb{C}^3$ is topologically trivial

plain: Slide a pinch point through a family: if one number stays fixed, its shape never changes

beats.text: A family $f_t$ of singularities in $\mathbb{C}^3$ whose Milnor number never changes
Lê–Ramanujam settled every other dimension; surfaces were the gap
Claimed: homeomorphisms carry each $f_t$ back to $f_0$

achievement.label: Lê–Ramanujam problem for surfaces (1976)
achievement.context: Before: Lê–Ramanujam (1976) proved $n \ne 3$ by h-cobordism; surfaces in $\mathbb{C}^3$ were open
achievement.note: Surfaces in $\mathbb{C}^3$ were the one remaining case

verify.ourCheck: We read the claim and caveats; we did not check the proof

voice.text: If the Milnor number stays constant, the topology should stay too.
Lê and Ramanujam proved every case except surfaces in complex three-space.
Claimed: true for surfaces in three-space as well.

sources.quote: Lê–Ramanujam (Amer. J. Math. 1976) proved topological triviality of μ-constant families for n ≠ 3
Surface case only (the remaining case). 37 pp. No Lean.
